User.title: User
User.description: Represents a user within the UniQueue system, including staff, department administrators, and superadmins, with specific roles and associated department access.

id.description: Unique identifier for the User entity.

name.description: The full name of the user.

role.description: The role of the user, defining their access level within the system. (Possible values: Superadmin, DeptAdmin, Staff)

departmentId.description: Reference to the Department this user belongs to. (Relationship: Department 1:N User). This is optional for 'Superadmin' roles.

Department.title: Department
Department.description: Represents a university department that utilizes the queueing system, defining its name and the services it offers.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Department entity.

name.description: The official name of the department (e.g., 'Main Building', 'IS', 'SOM').

hasAccounting.description: Indicates whether this department offers Accounting services in addition to Cashier services.

Counter.title: Counter
Counter.description: Represents a staff-bound counter instance within a department. Multiple staff accounts may share the same physical windowNumber while remaining distinct documents, and routing is enforced by the shared window range plus the route bucket.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Counter entity.

departmentId.description: Reference to the Department this counter belongs to. (Relationship: Department 1:N Counter)

counterNumber.description: The distinct number identifying this counter within its department.

windowNumber.description: The shared physical window number visible to students and staff. Multiple counter documents may point to the same windowNumber.

serviceType.description: The type of service provided at this counter. (Possible values: Cashier, Accounting)

routingDepartment.description: The route bucket enforced for this counter. (Possible values: Registrar, Accounting/Cashier)

currentStatus.description: The current operational status of the counter. (Possible values: Online, Offline, Serving, Vacant)

assignedStaffId.description: Reference to the User (Staff role) currently assigned to this counter. (Relationship: User 1:N Counter). This field is optional.

Ticket.title: Ticket
Ticket.description: Represents a single queue ticket generated by a student, tracking its service type, route bucket, status, and timestamps.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Ticket entity.

queueNumber.description: The displayable queue number for the ticket (e.g., C-001, A-001).

serviceType.description: The type of service requested for this ticket. (Possible values: Cashier, Accounting)

routingDepartment.description: The route bucket assigned to this ticket. (Possible values: Registrar, Accounting/Cashier)

status.description: The current status of the ticket in the queue lifecycle. (Possible values: Waiting, Called, Serving, Completed, NoShow)

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the ticket was created.

servedAt.description: Timestamp when the ticket started being served by a counter. This field is optional and populated once serving begins.

departmentId.description: Reference to the Department the ticket was issued for. (Relationship: Department 1:N Ticket)

counterId.description: Reference to the Counter currently serving or that served this ticket. (Relationship: Counter 1:N Ticket). This field is optional until the ticket is called or served.

definition.description: Dedicated collection to identify Superadmin users. The existence of a document for a given userId in this collection grants global Superadmin privileges. This adheres to the 'Existence over Content' DBAC principle. Document content is minimal, typically just the userId.

Stores user profiles for all system users (Superadmin, DeptAdmin, Staff, and Kiosk devices). Includes 'role' and 'departmentId' (optional for Superadmin, mandatory for DeptAdmin/Staff/Kiosk) which are crucial for database-backed access control. This document is the single source of truth for a user's permissions and departmental scope. Includes denormalized 'role' and 'departmentId' for authorization independence on the requesting user's profile.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user, typically matching Firebase Authentication UID (request.auth.uid).

definition.description: Stores definitions for each university department, including its name and whether it offers accounting services. Access is controlled by user roles (Superadmin, DeptAdmin) and their associated departmentId. This collection does not contain denormalized authorization fields as its own access is determined by the requesting user's credentials.

params.name: departmentId
params.description: The unique identifier for the department.

definition.description: Represents individual service counters organized under their respective departments. Documents in this subcollection include denormalized 'departmentId' (matching the parent path parameter) and 'assignedStaffId' for authorization independence and efficient rule evaluation. This structure ensures QAP compliance for department-scoped listing.

params.name: departmentId
params.description: The unique identifier of the parent department.

params.name: counterId
params.description: The unique identifier for the counter within the department.

definition.description: Stores queue tickets, organized under their respective departments. Each ticket document includes denormalized 'departmentId' (matching the parent path parameter) and 'serviceType' for robust, authorization-independent access control and efficient querying. This structure facilitates QAP-compliant list operations for kiosks, public monitors, and staff within their assigned departmental and service scope.

params.name: departmentId
params.description: The unique identifier of the parent department.

params.name: ticketId
params.description: The unique identifier for the ticket within the department.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure for the UniQueue system is designed with a strong emphasis on security, scalability, and debuggability, adhering to the core design principles.

Authorization Independence:
This design minimizes hierarchical authorization dependencies, especially avoiding get() calls that would break atomic operations.
User Roles and Department Assignment: User-specific authorization context (role, departmentId) is stored directly within each user's document at /users/{userId}. This allows Firebase Security Rules to evaluate request.auth.uid's permissions by performing a single, permissible get() operation on the requesting user's own profile. This is not a hierarchical dependency on the resource being accessed, thus maintaining authorization independence for resource access.
Denormalization for Nested Data: For Counter and Ticket entities, the departmentId is explicitly denormalized into each document. For instance, a Counter document in /departments/{departmentId}/counters/{counterId} will contain resource.data.departmentId, making it unnecessary to get() the parent Department document to check departmental authorization. Similarly, Ticket documents contain resource.data.departmentId and resource.data.serviceType, crucial for specific service queue management. assignedStaffId in Counter documents allows direct checks for staff ownership. This denormalization ensures that rules can operate atomically and efficiently without cross-document reads for authorization.

QAPs (Rules are not Filters):
The structural segregation and hierarchical paths are central to enabling secure and QAP-compliant list operations.
Department-Scoped Collections: Counters and Tickets are organized as subcollections under /departments/{departmentId}/. This hierarchical structure allows security rules to enforce list operations where the departmentId in the path (e.g., {departmentId} wildcard) must match the departmentId associated with the authenticated user (request.auth.uid). For example, a Department Admin user for department X can only list documents within /departments/X/counters because the rule explicitly checks that the {departmentId} in the path matches their own departmentId. This prevents unauthorized cross-departmental listing and ensures rules effectively enforce filtering, rather than relying on client-side filters.
Global Access for Superadmins: Superadmins are granted list access across top-level collections (e.g., /users, /departments) and blanket read/list access across all nested subcollections, ensuring their global oversight mandate is met.

DBAC (No Custom Claims):
Role-Based Access Control is entirely database-driven. A dedicated collection /roles_superadmin/{userId} is used where the existence of a document for a given userId grants Superadmin privileges. For other roles (DeptAdmin, Staff, and Kiosk devices), the role and departmentId are stored within their respective /users/{userId} documents. Authorization rules then check these database-resident roles and associated departmentId values against request.auth.uid without relying on custom JWT claims.

Structural Segregation & Access Modeling:
All documents within a given collection or subcollection (/departments/{departmentId}/counters, /departments/{departmentId}/tickets) share a homogeneous security posture (e.g., department-scoped access), simplifying rule logic.
Path-based ownership is used for user-specific data (/users/{userId}). Hierarchical paths (/departments/{departmentId}/counters, /departments/{departmentId}/tickets) are used for entities with strong 1:N relationships to departments, enabling clear and robust ownership-based security.

Kiosk Device Authorization:
To enable Kiosks to directly create tickets while adhering to DBAC and "No Custom Claims," Kiosk devices are treated as a special type of User. Each Kiosk authenticates with a unique request.auth.uid that maps to a document in /users/{kioskId}. This kioskId's role would be designated as 'Kiosk', and its associated departmentId would be stored directly in its /users/{kioskId} document. This allows ticket creation rules to securely verify resource.data.departmentId against the Kiosk's configured departmentId.

This comprehensive structure provides a secure, flexible, and easily debuggable foundation for the UniQueue system's authorization model.
